finding.requirement: A legitimate pending Connect must not fail solely because unrelated prior polling consumed a connection-wide transport budget; cancellation must settle honestly.
finding.consumer: RuntimeHost._oauth_flow -> NativeOAuth.operate -> exact pinned _codex_full_login_worker/_codex_poll_authorization AST -> FixedClient -> real HTTPX/HTTPcore -> local verified TLS over UDS -> start_auth_forwarder.
finding.concrete_case: Native interval 3s, repeated HTTP 403 pending replies, fifth poll delayed 4s. Each request remains below its 15s request timeout, but the pooled polling connection has a 15s total relay lifetime. Baseline cuts the in-flight fifth poll at 18.127s from flow start after a real local CHALLENGE observation.
finding.cause: FixedClient retains HTTP/1.1 connections across polls. start_auth_forwarder applies asyncio.timeout(15) around the whole auth.openai.com connection, including all prior requests and idle polling time. A later otherwise-valid response can cross that connection deadline and terminate the no-retry native worker.
finding.fix: Set httpx.Limits(max_keepalive_connections=0) on the existing FixedClient HTTPTransport. Each completed response retires its connection, so the next poll does not inherit the previous polling connection's remaining lifetime.
finding.why_management_oauth_edit_is_in_scope: The native producer intentionally reuses one client for polling. The reproduced mismatch is at that client's pooling seam, not in lease renewal, API/PG, UI or the native overlay. A single transport setting fixes the demonstrated case without changing any relay limit or native producer.

limits: This demonstrates one deterministic product defect, not the exclusive cause of the historical provider failure.
The recorded historical browser failure occurred sooner than this 18s reproduction. Historical root cause remains UNKNOWN.
The healthy immediate-response pooled control completed six polls and cancelled successfully, so connection age alone does not imply every pending flow fails at 15s.
The singleton/half-close hypothesis is not established as a product defect. _copy already propagates write_eof; its gather and admission semantics were not changed.
No claim that every possible OAuth failure or gap is removed. Additional TLS handshakes and DNS resolutions per poll are the intentional tradeoff.
